ko.title: [농업 101 #11] 작물은 왜 병에 걸릴까? 식물 질병과 방제 완벽 가이드

segments.src: > Plant diseases follow the same logic as human illness: a pathogen, a susceptible host, and the right conditions must line up — break any one link and the disease fails to spread.
segments.tr: > 식물 질병은 인간 질병과 같은 논리를 따릅니다: 병원체, 감수성 있는 숙주, 그리고 적절한 조건이 모두 맞아떨어져야 합니다 — 이 중 한 고리라도 끊기면 질병은 확산되지 않습니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: When a tomato leaf develops brown spots or a wheat field turns rusty orange, that is a plant disease at work.
segments.tr: 토마토 잎에 갈색 반점이 생기거나 밀밭이 녹슬은 주황색으로 변할 때, 이것은 식물 질병이 작동하는 것입니다.

segments.src: Most crop diseases are caused by three main groups of **pathogens** (disease-causing organisms):
segments.tr: 대부분의 작물 질병은 세 가지 주요 **병원체**(질병 유발 생물) 그룹에 의해 발생합니다:

segments.src: - **Fungi** — by far the most common. They cause blights, mildews, rusts, and rots. Fungi love warm, humid, wet conditions and spread by microscopic spores.
segments.tr: - **곰팡이** — 가장 흔합니다. 묘죽음병, 흰가루병, 녹병, 부패를 일으킵니다. 곰팡이는 따뜻하고 습한 젖은 조건을 좋아하며 현미경 크기의 포자로 확산됩니다.

segments.src: - **Bacteria** — cause wilts, spots, and soft rots. They need a wound or a natural opening (like a leaf pore) to get in, and thrive in warm, wet weather.
segments.tr: - **세균** — 시들음병, 반점, 연부부패를 일으킵니다. 침입하기 위해 상처나 자연 개구부(잎 기공 같은)가 필요하며 따뜻하고 습한 날씨에서 번성합니다.

segments.src: - **Viruses** — cause mottling, yellowing, and stunting. They cannot move on their own; they hitch a ride, usually inside an insect like an aphid, or on contaminated tools and hands.
segments.tr: - **바이러스** — 반점화, 황화, 왜소화를 일으킵니다. 스스로 이동할 수 없으며 주로 진딧물 같은 곤충 내부나 오염된 도구와 손에 얹혀 다닙니다.

segments.src: For any disease to actually happen, three things must come together at the same time.
segments.tr: 실제로 질병이 발생하려면 세 가지가 동시에 함께 나타나야 합니다.

segments.src: Plant scientists call this the **disease triangle**:
segments.tr: 식물 과학자들은 이를 **질병 삼각형**이라고 부릅니다:

segments.src: Susceptible host  +  Virulent pathogen  +  Favorable environment  =  Disease
segments.tr: Susceptible host  +  Virulent pathogen  +  Favorable environment  =  Disease

segments.src: If the plant is naturally resistant, or the pathogen is absent, or the weather is too dry or too cold, the disease does not develop.
segments.tr: 식물이 자연적으로 저항성이 있거나 병원체가 없거나 날씨가 너무 건조하거나 너무 추우면 질병은 발생하지 않습니다.

segments.src: This is the single most useful idea in all of plant protection, because it tells you exactly where to intervene: remove any one side of the triangle and you stop the disease.
segments.tr: 이것은 식물 보호의 모든 분야에서 가장 유용한 개념입니다. 왜냐하면 정확히 어디에 개입해야 하는지 알려주기 때문입니다: 삼각형의 어느 한 변이라도 제거하면 질병을 멈출 수 있습니다.

segments.src: **Transmission routes** — how pathogens travel — matter just as much as the pathogen itself.
segments.tr: **전파 경로** — 병원체가 이동하는 방식 — 병원체 자체만큼 중요합니다.

segments.src: Spores blow in on the **wind**; bacteria splash from soil onto leaves in the **rain**; viruses ride inside **insect vectors**; and all three can travel on **infected seed, transplants, tools, boots, and irrigation water**.
segments.tr: 포자는 **바람**에 날려오고; 세균은 **빗**으로 흙에서 잎으로 튀어오르며; 바이러스는 **곤충 매개체** 내부에서 이동합니다; 그리고 셋 모두 **감염된 종자, 묘, 도구, 부츠, 관개수**로 이동할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Knowing the route tells you where to build a barrier.
segments.tr: 경로를 알면 어디에 방벽을 구축해야 하는지 알 수 있습니다.

segments.src: A smart **control strategy** almost never relies on a single weapon.
segments.tr: 현명한 **방제 전략**은 거의 절대 단일 방법에만 의존하지 않습니다.

segments.src: Modern farming uses **Integrated Pest Management (IPM)** — layering several tactics so that no one method has to do all the work:
segments.tr: 현대 농업은 **통합 병해충 관리(IPM)**를 사용합니다 — 여러 전술을 겹겹이 적용하여 어떤 한 방법도 모든 일을 할 필요가 없게 합니다:

segments.src: 1. **Cultural control** — crop rotation, resistant varieties, proper spacing for airflow, and removing infected debris.
segments.tr: 1. **경종학적 방제** — 작물 윤작, 저항성 품종, 통풍을 위한 적절한 간격, 감염된 잔해 제거.

segments.src: 2. **Physical/mechanical control** — clean seed, sanitized tools, mulches, and pulling out diseased plants.
segments.tr: 2. **물리적/기계적 방제** — 깨끗한 종자, 소독된 도구, 멀칭, 병든 식물 제거.

segments.src: 3. **Biological control** — beneficial microbes or insects that suppress the pathogen or its vector.
segments.tr: 3. **생물 방제** — 병원체나 그 매개체를 억제하는 유익한 미생물이나 곤충.

segments.src: 4. **Chemical control** — fungicides or bactericides, used as a targeted last layer, not the first reflex.
segments.tr: 4. **화학 방제** — 살균제 또는 살균제, 첫 번째 반응이 아닌 표적화된 마지막 계층으로 사용됩니다.

segments.src: The goal is not to sterilize the field but to keep disease below the level where it hurts yield or quality.
segments.tr: 목표는 밭을 살균하는 것이 아니라 질병을 수확량이나 품질에 해를 끼치지 않는 수준 이하로 유지하는 것입니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상생활에서

segments.src: Picture a home gardener in Ohio growing tomatoes in a backyard raised bed.
segments.tr: 오하이오의 집 정원사가 뒷마당 높은 상자에서 토마토를 재배하는 것을 상상해 보세요.

segments.src: In late July, after a stretch of muggy, rainy days, the lower leaves show dark spots with yellow halos, then turn brown and drop.
segments.tr: 7월 말, 한동안 습하고 비 오는 날씨가 계속된 후 아래 잎에는 노란 테두리가 있는 검은 반점이 생기고 갈색으로 변해 떨어집니다.

segments.src: This is **early blight**, a fungal disease — a textbook case of the disease triangle snapping shut: a susceptible tomato (host), blight spores overwintering in the soil (pathogen), and warm, wet weather (environment).
segments.tr: 이것은 **조기 역병**, 곰팡이 질병입니다 — 질병 삼각형이 닫히는 교과서적 사례입니다: 감수성 있는 토마토(숙주), 흙에서 월동하는 역병 포자(병원체), 따뜻하고 습한 날씨(환경).

segments.src: Here is how IPM plays out on a small backyard budget, no lab required:
segments.tr: 작은 뒷마당 예산에서 IPM이 어떻게 작동하는지 보세요, 실험실이 필요 없습니다:

segments.src: - **Cultural:** Next season, plant the tomatoes in a different bed (rotation) and choose a blight-resistant variety at the local garden center. Space plants so air dries the leaves faster.
segments.tr: - **경종학적:** 다음 시즌에는 토마토를 다른 상자에 심고(윤작) 지역 정원 센터에서 역병 저항성 품종을 선택하세요. 공기가 잎을 더 빨리 말릴 수 있도록 식물 간격을 벌리세요.

segments.src: - **Physical:** Lay down mulch so rain does not splash soil-borne spores up onto the leaves, and water the roots — not the foliage — early in the day.
segments.tr: - **물리적:** 빗이 흙에서 나온 포자를 잎까지 튀지 않도록 멀칭을 깔고 하루 초반에 잎이 아닌 뿌리에 물을 주세요.

segments.src: - **Biological/Chemical:** If it spreads, an approved garden fungicide labeled for tomato blight can protect the healthy upper leaves; always follow the label rate.
segments.tr: - **생물학적/화학적:** 확산되면 토마토 역병용으로 승인된 정원 살균제가 건강한 위쪽 잎을 보호할 수 있습니다; 항상 라벨 용량을 따르세요.

segments.src: Scale that same thinking up and it is exactly what a commercial grower in California's Central Valley or an Iowa corn farmer does — just with weather forecasting, scouting reports, and disease-forecasting apps guiding the timing.
segments.tr: 같은 방식으로 규모를 확대하면 캘리포니아의 중앙 계곡의 상업 재배자나 아이오와의 옥수수 농부가 정확히 하는 것입니다 — 단지 날씨 예보, 조사 보고서, 질병 예측 앱이 시기를 안내할 뿐입니다.

segments.src: The principles are identical whether the field is 20 square feet or 2,000 acres.
segments.tr: 원칙은 밭이 20제곱피트이든 2,000에이커이든 동일합니다.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Crop diseases are caused mainly by fungi, bacteria, and viruses, each with its own transmission route (wind, water/splash, insects, or contaminated seed and tools).
segments.tr: 1. 작물 질병은 주로 곰팡이, 세균, 바이러스에 의해 발생하며, 각각 고유한 전파 경로(바람, 물/튀김, 곤충, 오염된 종자 및 도구)가 있습니다.

segments.src: 2. Disease only occurs when a susceptible host, an active pathogen, and a favorable environment overlap — the "disease triangle."
segments.tr: 2. 질병은 감수성 있는 숙주, 활동적인 병원체, 유리한 환경이 겹칠 때만 발생합니다 — "질병 삼각형".

segments.src: 3. The best defense is Integrated Pest Management: layer cultural, physical, biological, and chemical tactics rather than relying on any single one.
segments.tr: 3. 최고의 방어는 통합 병해충 관리입니다: 단일 방법에 의존하기보다는 경종학적, 물리적, 생물학적, 화학적 전술을 겹겹이 적용하세요.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 자가 진단 퀴즈

segments.src: 1. Which group of pathogens is the most common cause of crop diseases such as blights, mildews, and rusts?
segments.tr: 1. 역병, 흰가루병, 녹병 같은 작물 질병의 가장 흔한 원인인 병원체 그룹은 어느 것입니까?

segments.src: - A) Bacteria
segments.tr: - A) 세균

segments.src: - B) Fungi
segments.tr: - B) 곰팡이

segments.src: - C) Viruses
segments.tr: - C) 바이러스

segments.src: 2. According to the disease triangle, if the weather stays hot and dry (unfavorable to a moisture-loving pathogen), the disease will still break out. (O / X)
segments.tr: 2. 질병 삼각형에 따르면 날씨가 뜨겁고 건조하면(습기를 좋아하는 병원체에 불리우면) 질병이 여전히 발생합니다. (O / X)

segments.src: 3. Which of the following is a *cultural* control tactic?
segments.tr: 3. 다음 중 *경종학적* 방제 전술은 어느 것입니까?

segments.src: - A) Spraying a fungicide on infected leaves
segments.tr: - A) 감염된 잎에 살균제 분무하기

segments.src: - B) Rotating crops and planting a resistant variety
segments.tr: - B) 작물 윤작 및 저항성 품종 심기

segments.src: - C) Releasing predatory insects
segments.tr: - C) 포식성 곤충 방출하기

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Pathogen** — a disease-causing organism, such as a fungus, bacterium, or virus.
segments.tr: - **병원체** — 곰팡이, 세균, 또는 바이러스와 같은 질병 유발 생물.

segments.src: - **Disease triangle** — the principle that disease needs a susceptible host, a pathogen, and a favorable environment together.
segments.tr: - **질병 삼각형** — 질병이 감수성 있는 숙주, 병원체, 유리한 환경을 함께 필요로 한다는 원칙.

segments.src: - **Vector** — a carrier (often an insect like an aphid) that transmits a pathogen, especially viruses, from plant to plant.
segments.tr: - **매개체** — 진딧물 같은 곤충) 병원체, 특히 바이러스를 한 식물에서 다른 식물로 전파하는 매개자.

segments.src: - **Integrated Pest Management (IPM)** — a strategy that combines cultural, physical, biological, and chemical tactics to keep disease below a damaging level.
segments.tr: - **통합 병해충 관리(IPM)** — 경종학적, 물리적, 생물학적, 화학적 전술을 결합하여 질병을 해로운 수준 이하로 유지하는 전략.

segments.src: - **Resistant variety** — a crop type bred to be less susceptible to a specific disease.
segments.tr: - **저항성 품종** — 특정 질병에 덜 감수성이 되도록 육성된 작물 유형.

segments.src: *Answers: 1) B — Fungi cause the majority of crop diseases and spread easily by spores.
segments.tr: *답변: 1) B — 곰팡이는 대부분의 작물 질병을 일으키고 포자로 쉽게 확산됩니다.

segments.src: 2) X — False; if the environment is unfavorable, one side of the disease triangle is missing, so the disease does not develop.
segments.tr: 2) X — 거짓; 환경이 불리하면 질병 삼각형의 한 변이 없으므로 질병이 발생하지 않습니다.

segments.src: 3) B — Crop rotation and resistant varieties are cultural controls; fungicides are chemical and predatory insects are biological.*
segments.tr: 3) B — 작물 윤작과 저항성 품종은 경종학적 방제이고; 살균제는 화학 방제이며 포식성 곤충은 생물 방제입니다.*

zh.title: [农业 101 #11] 作物为什么会生病？植物病害和防治现场指南

segments.src: > Plant diseases follow the same logic as human illness: a pathogen, a susceptible host, and the right conditions must line up — break any one link and the disease fails to spread.
segments.tr: > 植物病害遵循与人类疾病相同的逻辑：病原体、易感宿主和适宜的环境条件必须同时具备——破坏其中任何一个环节，病害就无法传播。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: When a tomato leaf develops brown spots or a wheat field turns rusty orange, that is a plant disease at work.
segments.tr: 当番茄叶片上出现褐色斑点，或者小麦田变成锈红色时，植物病害就在发生。

segments.src: Most crop diseases are caused by three main groups of **pathogens** (disease-causing organisms):
segments.tr: 大多数作物病害由三大类**病原体**（导致疾病的生物）引起：

segments.src: - **Fungi** — by far the most common. They cause blights, mildews, rusts, and rots. Fungi love warm, humid, wet conditions and spread by microscopic spores.
segments.tr: - **真菌** —— 迄今为止最常见的。它们引起枯病、霉病、锈病和腐烂病。真菌喜欢温暖、潮湿的条件，通过显微镜下的孢子传播。

segments.src: - **Bacteria** — cause wilts, spots, and soft rots. They need a wound or a natural opening (like a leaf pore) to get in, and thrive in warm, wet weather.
segments.tr: - **细菌** —— 引起萎蔫、斑点和软腐烂。它们需要伤口或自然孔隙（如叶孔）才能进入，在温暖、潮湿的天气中繁殖。

segments.src: - **Viruses** — cause mottling, yellowing, and stunting. They cannot move on their own; they hitch a ride, usually inside an insect like an aphid, or on contaminated tools and hands.
segments.tr: - **病毒** —— 引起花叶、黄化和矮化。它们无法自行移动；它们搭便车，通常在蚜虫等昆虫体内，或通过受污染的工具和手传播。

segments.src: For any disease to actually happen, three things must come together at the same time.
segments.tr: 要使任何病害真正发生，三件事必须同时汇聚。

segments.src: Plant scientists call this the **disease triangle**:
segments.tr: 植物科学家称之为**病害三角形**：

segments.src: Susceptible host  +  Virulent pathogen  +  Favorable environment  =  Disease
segments.tr: Susceptible host  +  Virulent pathogen  +  Favorable environment  =  Disease

segments.src: If the plant is naturally resistant, or the pathogen is absent, or the weather is too dry or too cold, the disease does not develop.
segments.tr: 如果植物天然抗病，或病原体不存在，或天气过于干燥或寒冷，病害就不会发展。

segments.src: This is the single most useful idea in all of plant protection, because it tells you exactly where to intervene: remove any one side of the triangle and you stop the disease.
segments.tr: 这是植物保护中最有用的单一理念，因为它准确告诉你在哪里进行干预：移除三角形的任何一条边，你就能阻止病害。

segments.src: **Transmission routes** — how pathogens travel — matter just as much as the pathogen itself.
segments.tr: **传播途径** —— 病原体如何传播 —— 其重要性与病原体本身一样。

segments.src: Spores blow in on the **wind**; bacteria splash from soil onto leaves in the **rain**; viruses ride inside **insect vectors**; and all three can travel on **infected seed, transplants, tools, boots, and irrigation water**.
segments.tr: 孢子通过**风**吹来；细菌通过**雨**从土壤溅到叶片上；病毒乘坐**昆虫媒介**；这三种都可以通过**带病种子、秧苗、工具、靴子和灌溉水**传播。

segments.src: Knowing the route tells you where to build a barrier.
segments.tr: 了解传播途径可以告诉你在哪里建立防线。

segments.src: A smart **control strategy** almost never relies on a single weapon.
segments.tr: 明智的**防治策略**几乎从不依赖单一的方法。

segments.src: Modern farming uses **Integrated Pest Management (IPM)** — layering several tactics so that no one method has to do all the work:
segments.tr: 现代农业采用**综合虫害管理 (IPM)** —— 叠加多种策略，这样没有一种方法需要承担所有工作：

segments.src: 1. **Cultural control** — crop rotation, resistant varieties, proper spacing for airflow, and removing infected debris.
segments.tr: 1. **农业防治** —— 轮作、抗病品种、合理密植以促进通风，以及清除受感染的残留物。

segments.src: 2. **Physical/mechanical control** — clean seed, sanitized tools, mulches, and pulling out diseased plants.
segments.tr: 2. **物理/机械防治** —— 无菌种子、消毒的工具、覆盖物，以及清除患病植株。

segments.src: 3. **Biological control** — beneficial microbes or insects that suppress the pathogen or its vector.
segments.tr: 3. **生物防治** —— 有益微生物或昆虫，抑制病原体或其媒介。

segments.src: 4. **Chemical control** — fungicides or bactericides, used as a targeted last layer, not the first reflex.
segments.tr: 4. **化学防治** —— 杀菌剂或杀菌剂，作为有针对性的最后手段使用，而非首选。

segments.src: The goal is not to sterilize the field but to keep disease below the level where it hurts yield or quality.
segments.tr: 目标不是灭菌田地，而是将病害控制在不损害产量或质量的水平以下。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活中

segments.src: Picture a home gardener in Ohio growing tomatoes in a backyard raised bed.
segments.tr: 想象一位俄亥俄州的家庭园丁在后院高垄种植番茄。

segments.src: In late July, after a stretch of muggy, rainy days, the lower leaves show dark spots with yellow halos, then turn brown and drop.
segments.tr: 在七月下旬，经过一段潮湿多雨的日子后，下层叶片显示出带有黄色晕轮的深色斑点，然后变褐色并脱落。

segments.src: This is **early blight**, a fungal disease — a textbook case of the disease triangle snapping shut: a susceptible tomato (host), blight spores overwintering in the soil (pathogen), and warm, wet weather (environment).
segments.tr: 这是**早疫病**，一种真菌病害 —— 病害三角形闭合的典型案例：易感番茄（宿主）、在土壤中越冬的疫病孢子（病原体）和温暖潮湿的天气（环境）。

segments.src: Here is how IPM plays out on a small backyard budget, no lab required:
segments.tr: 以下是 IPM 在小型后院预算上的展开方式，无需实验室：

segments.src: - **Cultural:** Next season, plant the tomatoes in a different bed (rotation) and choose a blight-resistant variety at the local garden center. Space plants so air dries the leaves faster.
segments.tr: - **农业防治：**下一季，在不同的床上种植番茄（轮作）并在当地园艺中心选择抗疫病品种。间距种植以便空气更快地干燥叶片。

segments.src: - **Physical:** Lay down mulch so rain does not splash soil-borne spores up onto the leaves, and water the roots — not the foliage — early in the day.
segments.tr: - **物理防治：**铺设覆盖物，防止雨水将土壤中的孢子溅到叶片上，并在一天早期浇根部 —— 而非叶片。

segments.src: - **Biological/Chemical:** If it spreads, an approved garden fungicide labeled for tomato blight can protect the healthy upper leaves; always follow the label rate.
segments.tr: - **生物/化学防治：**如果病害传播，标明适用于番茄疫病的已批准园用杀菌剂可以保护健康的上层叶片；始终遵循标签用量。

segments.src: Scale that same thinking up and it is exactly what a commercial grower in California's Central Valley or an Iowa corn farmer does — just with weather forecasting, scouting reports, and disease-forecasting apps guiding the timing.
segments.tr: 将这一思路扩大，这正是加州中央谷地的商业种植者或爱荷华州玉米农民所做的 —— 只是由天气预报、侦察报告和病害预报应用程序指导时间安排。

segments.src: The principles are identical whether the field is 20 square feet or 2,000 acres.
segments.tr: 无论田地是 20 平方英尺还是 2,000 英亩，原则是相同的。

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. Crop diseases are caused mainly by fungi, bacteria, and viruses, each with its own transmission route (wind, water/splash, insects, or contaminated seed and tools).
segments.tr: 1. 作物病害主要由真菌、细菌和病毒引起，每种都有自己的传播途径（风、水/溅溅、昆虫，或受污染的种子和工具）。

segments.src: 2. Disease only occurs when a susceptible host, an active pathogen, and a favorable environment overlap — the "disease triangle."
segments.tr: 2. 只有当易感宿主、活性病原体和有利环境重叠时，病害才会发生 —— "病害三角形"。

segments.src: 3. The best defense is Integrated Pest Management: layer cultural, physical, biological, and chemical tactics rather than relying on any single one.
segments.tr: 3. 最佳防御是综合虫害管理：叠加农业、物理、生物和化学策略，而非依赖单一策略。

segments.tr: ## ✅ 自测小题

segments.tr: 1. 以下哪组病原体最常见是引起枯病、霉病和锈病等作物病害的原因？

segments.src: - A) Bacteria
segments.tr: - A) 细菌

segments.tr: - C) 病毒

segments.tr: - A) 在受感染的叶片上喷洒杀菌剂

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Pathogen** — a disease-causing organism, such as a fungus, bacterium, or virus.
segments.tr: - **病原体** —— 导致疾病的生物，如真菌、细菌或病毒。

segments.src: - **Disease triangle** — the principle that disease needs a susceptible host, a pathogen, and a favorable environment together.
segments.tr: - **病害三角形** —— 病害需要易感宿主、病原体和有利环境共同存在的原则。

segments.src: - **Vector** — a carrier (often an insect like an aphid) that transmits a pathogen, especially viruses, from plant to plant.
segments.tr: - **媒介** —— 载体（通常是蚜虫等昆虫），将病原体，特别是病毒，从植物传播到植物。

segments.src: - **Integrated Pest Management (IPM)** — a strategy that combines cultural, physical, biological, and chemical tactics to keep disease below a damaging level.
segments.tr: - **综合虫害管理 (IPM)** —— 结合农业、物理、生物和化学策略以将病害控制在有害水平以下的策略。

segments.src: - **Resistant variety** — a crop type bred to be less susceptible to a specific disease.
segments.tr: - **抗病品种** —— 为减少对特定病害敏感性而育种的作物类型。

segments.src: *Answers: 1) B — Fungi cause the majority of crop diseases and spread easily by spores.
segments.tr: *答案：1) B — 真菌导致大多数作物病害，并通过孢子容易传播。

segments.src: 2) X — False; if the environment is unfavorable, one side of the disease triangle is missing, so the disease does not develop.
segments.tr: 2) X — 错误；如果环境不利，病害三角形的一条边就会缺失，所以病害不会发展。

segments.src: 3) B — Crop rotation and resistant varieties are cultural controls; fungicides are chemical and predatory insects are biological.*
segments.tr: 3) B — 轮作和抗病品种是农业防治；杀菌剂是化学防治，捕食性昆虫是生物防治。*

hi.title: [कृषि 101 #11] फसलें बीमार क्यों होती हैं? पौधों की बीमारी और नियंत्रण के लिए एक क्षेत्र मार्गदर्शक

segments.src: > Plant diseases follow the same logic as human illness: a pathogen, a susceptible host, and the right conditions must line up — break any one link and the disease fails to spread.
segments.tr: > पौधों की बीमारियां मानव रोग के समान तर्क का पालन करती हैं: एक रोगाणु, एक संवेदनशील मेजबान, और सही परिस्थितियां एक साथ होनी चाहिए — किसी भी एक कड़ी को तोड़ें और बीमारी फैलने में विफल हो जाती है।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: When a tomato leaf develops brown spots or a wheat field turns rusty orange, that is a plant disease at work.
segments.tr: जब एक टमाटर की पत्ती भूरे धब्बे विकसित करती है या एक गेहूं का खेत जंग खाए हुए नारंगी रंग में बदल जाता है, तो यह एक पौधे की बीमारी काम में है।

segments.src: Most crop diseases are caused by three main groups of **pathogens** (disease-causing organisms):
segments.tr: अधिकांश फसल रोग **रोगाणुओं** (बीमारी पैदा करने वाले जीव) के तीन मुख्य समूहों के कारण होते हैं:

segments.src: - **Fungi** — by far the most common. They cause blights, mildews, rusts, and rots. Fungi love warm, humid, wet conditions and spread by microscopic spores.
segments.tr: - **कवक** — अब तक सबसे आम। वे अनावृत, फफूंदी, जंग और सड़न का कारण बनते हैं। कवक गर्म, आर्द्र, गीली परिस्थितियों को पसंद करते हैं और सूक्ष्म बीजाणुओं से फैलते हैं।

segments.src: - **Bacteria** — cause wilts, spots, and soft rots. They need a wound or a natural opening (like a leaf pore) to get in, and thrive in warm, wet weather.
segments.tr: - **बैक्टीरिया** — मुरझाने, धब्बे और नरम सड़न का कारण बनते हैं। उन्हें प्रवेश करने के लिए एक घाव या एक प्राकृतिक उद्घाटन (जैसे एक पत्ती का छिद्र) की आवश्यकता होती है, और गर्म, गीले मौसम में पनपते हैं।

segments.src: - **Viruses** — cause mottling, yellowing, and stunting. They cannot move on their own; they hitch a ride, usually inside an insect like an aphid, or on contaminated tools and hands.
segments.tr: - **वायरस** — धब्बेदारपन, पीलापन और बौनापन का कारण बनते हैं। वे अपने आप नहीं चल सकते; वे सवारी करते हैं, आमतौर पर एक कीट जैसे एफिड के अंदर, या दूषित उपकरणों और हाथों पर।

segments.src: For any disease to actually happen, three things must come together at the same time.
segments.tr: किसी भी बीमारी के वास्तव में होने के लिए, तीन चीजें एक ही समय में एक साथ आनी चाहिए।

segments.src: Plant scientists call this the **disease triangle**:
segments.tr: पौधों के वैज्ञानिक इसे **रोग त्रिभुज** कहते हैं:

segments.src: Susceptible host  +  Virulent pathogen  +  Favorable environment  =  Disease
segments.tr: Susceptible host  +  Virulent pathogen  +  Favorable environment  =  Disease

segments.src: If the plant is naturally resistant, or the pathogen is absent, or the weather is too dry or too cold, the disease does not develop.
segments.tr: यदि पौधा स्वाभाविक रूप से प्रतिरोधी है, या रोगाणु अनुपस्थित है, या मौसम बहुत सूखा या बहुत ठंडा है, तो बीमारी विकसित नहीं होती है।

segments.src: This is the single most useful idea in all of plant protection, because it tells you exactly where to intervene: remove any one side of the triangle and you stop the disease.
segments.tr: यह पौधे की सुरक्षा में सबसे उपयोगी विचार है, क्योंकि यह आपको बताता है कि सही जगह पर हस्तक्षेप कहां करें: त्रिभुज की कोई भी एक भुजा हटाएं और आप बीमारी को रोक देते हैं।

segments.src: **Transmission routes** — how pathogens travel — matter just as much as the pathogen itself.
segments.tr: **संचरण मार्ग** — कैसे रोगाणु यात्रा करते हैं — रोगाणु के समान ही महत्वपूर्ण हैं।

segments.src: Spores blow in on the **wind**; bacteria splash from soil onto leaves in the **rain**; viruses ride inside **insect vectors**; and all three can travel on **infected seed, transplants, tools, boots, and irrigation water**.
segments.tr: बीजाणु **हवा** में उड़ते हैं; बैक्टीरिया **बारिश** में मिट्टी से पत्तियों पर छिटकते हैं; वायरस **कीट वाहकों** के अंदर सवारी करते हैं; और सभी तीन **संक्रमित बीज, प्रत्यारोपण, उपकरण, जूते और सिंचाई जल** पर यात्रा कर सकते हैं।

segments.src: Knowing the route tells you where to build a barrier.
segments.tr: मार्ग जानने से पता चलता है कि अवरोध कहां बनाना है।

segments.src: A smart **control strategy** almost never relies on a single weapon.
segments.tr: एक स्मार्ट **नियंत्रण रणनीति** लगभग कभी भी एक एकल हथियार पर निर्भर नहीं करती है।

segments.src: Modern farming uses **Integrated Pest Management (IPM)** — layering several tactics so that no one method has to do all the work:
segments.tr: आधुनिक कृषि **एकीकृत कीट प्रबंधन (IPM)** का उपयोग करती है — कई रणनीतियों को परत करना ताकि कोई भी विधि सभी काम न करे:

segments.src: 1. **Cultural control** — crop rotation, resistant varieties, proper spacing for airflow, and removing infected debris.
segments.tr: 1. **सांस्कृतिक नियंत्रण** — फसल चक्र, प्रतिरोधी किस्में, वायु प्रवाह के लिए उचित दूरी, और संक्रमित मलबे को हटाना।

segments.src: 2. **Physical/mechanical control** — clean seed, sanitized tools, mulches, and pulling out diseased plants.
segments.tr: 2. **भौतिक/यांत्रिक नियंत्रण** — स्वच्छ बीज, कीटाणुरहित उपकरण, मल्च, और बीमार पौधों को निकालना।

segments.src: 3. **Biological control** — beneficial microbes or insects that suppress the pathogen or its vector.
segments.tr: 3. **जैविक नियंत्रण** — लाभकारी सूक्ष्मजीव या कीट जो रोगाणु या इसके वाहक को दबाते हैं।

segments.src: 4. **Chemical control** — fungicides or bactericides, used as a targeted last layer, not the first reflex.
segments.tr: 4. **रासायनिक नियंत्रण** — कवकनाशी या जीवाणुनाशी, एक लक्षित अंतिम परत के रूप में उपयोग किया जाता है, पहली प्रतिक्रिया नहीं।

segments.src: The goal is not to sterilize the field but to keep disease below the level where it hurts yield or quality.
segments.tr: लक्ष्य खेत को कीटाणुरहित करना नहीं है बल्कि बीमारी को उस स्तर से नीचे रखना है जहां यह उपज या गुणवत्ता को नुकसान पहुंचाता है।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोजमर्रा की जिंदगी में

segments.src: Picture a home gardener in Ohio growing tomatoes in a backyard raised bed.
segments.tr: ओहायो में एक गृह माली की कल्पना करें जो एक आंगन के ऊंचे बिस्तर में टमाटर उगा रहा है।

segments.src: In late July, after a stretch of muggy, rainy days, the lower leaves show dark spots with yellow halos, then turn brown and drop.
segments.tr: जुलाई के अंत में, उमस भरे, बरसात के दिनों के बाद, निचली पत्तियों पर पीली आभा के साथ गहरे धब्बे दिखाई देते हैं, फिर भूरे हो जाते हैं और गिर जाते हैं।

segments.src: This is **early blight**, a fungal disease — a textbook case of the disease triangle snapping shut: a susceptible tomato (host), blight spores overwintering in the soil (pathogen), and warm, wet weather (environment).
segments.tr: यह **शुरुआती अनावृत** है, एक कवक रोग — रोग त्रिभुज के बंद होने का एक पाठ्यपुस्तक केस: एक संवेदनशील टमाटर (मेजबान), मिट्टी में सर्दियों में बीजाणु (रोगाणु), और गर्म, गीली जलवायु (पर्यावरण)।

segments.src: Here is how IPM plays out on a small backyard budget, no lab required:
segments.tr: यहाँ एक छोटे आंगन बजट पर IPM कैसे काम करता है, कोई लैब आवश्यक नहीं:

segments.src: - **Cultural:** Next season, plant the tomatoes in a different bed (rotation) and choose a blight-resistant variety at the local garden center. Space plants so air dries the leaves faster.
segments.tr: - **सांस्कृतिक:** अगले मौसम में, टमाटरों को एक अलग बिस्तर (चक्र) में लगाएं और स्थानीय उद्यान केंद्र में एक अनावृत-प्रतिरोधी किस्म चुनें। पौधों को इस तरह दूर रखें कि हवा पत्तियों को तेजी से सूख जाए।

segments.src: - **Physical:** Lay down mulch so rain does not splash soil-borne spores up onto the leaves, and water the roots — not the foliage — early in the day.
segments.tr: - **भौतिक:** मल्च बिछाएं ताकि बारिश मिट्टी से पैदा होने वाले बीजाणुओं को पत्तियों पर न छिटकाए, और जड़ों को पानी दें — न कि पत्तियों को — दिन की शुरुआत में।

segments.src: - **Biological/Chemical:** If it spreads, an approved garden fungicide labeled for tomato blight can protect the healthy upper leaves; always follow the label rate.
segments.tr: - **जैविक/रासायनिक:** यदि यह फैलता है, तो टमाटर अनावृत के लिए लेबल किया गया एक अनुमोदित बगीचे कवकनाशी स्वस्थ ऊपरी पत्तियों की रक्षा कर सकता है; हमेशा लेबल दर का पालन करें।

segments.src: Scale that same thinking up and it is exactly what a commercial grower in California's Central Valley or an Iowa corn farmer does — just with weather forecasting, scouting reports, and disease-forecasting apps guiding the timing.

es.title: [Agricultura 101 #11] ¿Por Qué Se Enferman los Cultivos? Una Guía de Campo para Enfermedades de Plantas y Control

segments.src: > Plant diseases follow the same logic as human illness: a pathogen, a susceptible host, and the right conditions must line up — break any one link and the disease fails to spread.
segments.tr: > Las enfermedades de las plantas siguen la misma lógica que las enfermedades humanas: un patógeno, un hospedero susceptible y las condiciones adecuadas deben alinearse — rompe cualquier eslabón y la enfermedad no se propaga.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de Hoy

segments.src: When a tomato leaf develops brown spots or a wheat field turns rusty orange, that is a plant disease at work.
segments.tr: Cuando una hoja de tomate desarrolla manchas marrones o un campo de trigo se vuelve de color naranja oxidado, esa es una enfermedad de plantas en acción.

segments.src: Most crop diseases are caused by three main groups of **pathogens** (disease-causing organisms):
segments.tr: La mayoría de las enfermedades de cultivos son causadas por tres grupos principales de **patógenos** (organismos causantes de enfermedades):

segments.src: - **Fungi** — by far the most common. They cause blights, mildews, rusts, and rots. Fungi love warm, humid, wet conditions and spread by microscopic spores.
segments.tr: - **Hongos** — con mucho, los más comunes. Causan tizones, mildius, royas y podredumbres. Los hongos aman las condiciones cálidas, húmedas y mojadas, y se propagan por esporas microscópicas.

segments.src: - **Bacteria** — cause wilts, spots, and soft rots. They need a wound or a natural opening (like a leaf pore) to get in, and thrive in warm, wet weather.
segments.tr: - **Bacterias** — causan marchitamiento, manchas y podredumbres blandas. Necesitan una herida o una abertura natural (como un poro foliar) para entrar, y prosperan en clima cálido y húmedo.

segments.src: - **Viruses** — cause mottling, yellowing, and stunting. They cannot move on their own; they hitch a ride, usually inside an insect like an aphid, or on contaminated tools and hands.
segments.tr: - **Virus** — causan manchado, amarillamiento y enanismo. No pueden moverse por sí solos; se transportan, generalmente dentro de un insecto como un áfido, o en herramientas y manos contaminadas.

segments.src: For any disease to actually happen, three things must come together at the same time.
segments.tr: Para que cualquier enfermedad ocurra realmente, tres cosas deben ocurrir al mismo tiempo.

segments.src: Plant scientists call this the **disease triangle**:
segments.tr: Los científicos de plantas llaman a esto el **triángulo de la enfermedad**:

segments.src: Susceptible host  +  Virulent pathogen  +  Favorable environment  =  Disease
segments.tr: Susceptible host  +  Virulent pathogen  +  Favorable environment  =  Disease

segments.src: If the plant is naturally resistant, or the pathogen is absent, or the weather is too dry or too cold, the disease does not develop.
segments.tr: Si la planta es naturalmente resistente, o el patógeno está ausente, o el clima es demasiado seco o demasiado frío, la enfermedad no se desarrolla.

segments.src: This is the single most useful idea in all of plant protection, because it tells you exactly where to intervene: remove any one side of the triangle and you stop the disease.
segments.tr: Este es el concepto más útil en toda la protección de plantas, porque te dice exactamente dónde intervenir: elimina cualquier lado del triángulo y la enfermedad desaparece.

segments.src: **Transmission routes** — how pathogens travel — matter just as much as the pathogen itself.
segments.tr: **Las vías de transmisión** — cómo viajan los patógenos — son tan importantes como el patógeno mismo.

segments.src: Spores blow in on the **wind**; bacteria splash from soil onto leaves in the **rain**; viruses ride inside **insect vectors**; and all three can travel on **infected seed, transplants, tools, boots, and irrigation water**.
segments.tr: Las esporas vuelan en el **viento**; las bacterias salpican del suelo a las hojas en la **lluvia**; los virus viajan dentro de **vectores de insectos**; y los tres pueden viajar en **semillas infectadas, trasplantes, herramientas, botas y agua de riego**.

segments.src: Knowing the route tells you where to build a barrier.
segments.tr: Conocer la vía de transmisión te dice dónde construir una barrera.

segments.src: A smart **control strategy** almost never relies on a single weapon.
segments.tr: Una **estrategia de control** inteligente casi nunca depende de una sola arma.

segments.src: Modern farming uses **Integrated Pest Management (IPM)** — layering several tactics so that no one method has to do all the work:
segments.tr: La agricultura moderna utiliza **Manejo Integrado de Plagas (MIP)** — combinando varias tácticas para que ningún método tenga que hacer todo el trabajo:

segments.src: 1. **Cultural control** — crop rotation, resistant varieties, proper spacing for airflow, and removing infected debris.
segments.tr: 1. **Control cultural** — rotación de cultivos, variedades resistentes, espaciamiento adecuado para la circulación del aire, y eliminación de residuos infectados.

segments.src: 2. **Physical/mechanical control** — clean seed, sanitized tools, mulches, and pulling out diseased plants.
segments.tr: 2. **Control físico/mecánico** — semillas limpias, herramientas sanitizadas, acolchados, y extracción de plantas enfermas.

segments.src: 3. **Biological control** — beneficial microbes or insects that suppress the pathogen or its vector.
segments.tr: 3. **Control biológico** — microbios o insectos beneficiosos que suprimen el patógeno o su vector.

segments.src: 4. **Chemical control** — fungicides or bactericides, used as a targeted last layer, not the first reflex.
segments.tr: 4. **Control químico** — fungicidas o bactericidas, utilizados como una capa final dirigida, no el primer reflejo.

segments.src: The goal is not to sterilize the field but to keep disease below the level where it hurts yield or quality.
segments.tr: El objetivo no es esterilizar el campo sino mantener la enfermedad por debajo del nivel donde afecta el rendimiento o la calidad.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la Vida Cotidiana

segments.src: Picture a home gardener in Ohio growing tomatoes in a backyard raised bed.
segments.tr: Imagina un jardinero casero en Ohio cultivando tomates en una cama elevada de su patio.

segments.src: In late July, after a stretch of muggy, rainy days, the lower leaves show dark spots with yellow halos, then turn brown and drop.
segments.tr: A finales de julio, después de un período de días bochornosos y lluviosos, las hojas inferiores muestran manchas oscuras con halos amarillos, luego se vuelven marrones y caen.

segments.src: This is **early blight**, a fungal disease — a textbook case of the disease triangle snapping shut: a susceptible tomato (host), blight spores overwintering in the soil (pathogen), and warm, wet weather (environment).
segments.tr: Este es el **tizón temprano**, una enfermedad fúngica — un ejemplo perfecto del triángulo de la enfermedad: un tomate susceptible (hospedero), esporas de tizón que invernan en el suelo (patógeno), y clima cálido y húmedo (ambiente).

segments.src: Here is how IPM plays out on a small backyard budget, no lab required:
segments.tr: Así es como el MIP se desarrolla en un presupuesto pequeño de patio trasero, sin laboratorio requerido:

segments.src: - **Cultural:** Next season, plant the tomatoes in a different bed (rotation) and choose a blight-resistant variety at the local garden center. Space plants so air dries the leaves faster.
segments.tr: - **Cultural:** La próxima temporada, planta los tomates en una cama diferente (rotación) y elige una variedad resistente al tizón en el centro de jardinería local. Espacía las plantas para que el aire seque las hojas más rápido.

segments.src: - **Physical:** Lay down mulch so rain does not splash soil-borne spores up onto the leaves, and water the roots — not the foliage — early in the day.
segments.tr: - **Físico:** Coloca acolchado para que la lluvia no salpique esporas del suelo hacia las hojas, y riega las raíces — no el follaje — temprano en el día.

segments.src: - **Biological/Chemical:** If it spreads, an approved garden fungicide labeled for tomato blight can protect the healthy upper leaves; always follow the label rate.
segments.tr: - **Biológico/Químico:** Si se propaga, un fungicida de jardín aprobado etiquetado para tizón de tomate puede proteger las hojas superiores sanas; siempre sigue la dosis de la etiqueta.

segments.src: Scale that same thinking up and it is exactly what a commercial grower in California's Central Valley or an Iowa corn farmer does — just with weather forecasting, scouting reports, and disease-forecasting apps guiding the timing.
segments.tr: Amplía ese mismo pensamiento y es exactamente lo que hace un productor comercial en el Valle Central de California o un agricultor de maíz de Iowa — solo con pronósticos del clima, informes de exploración, y aplicaciones de pronóstico de enfermedades guiando el momento.

segments.src: The principles are identical whether the field is 20 square feet or 2,000 acres.
segments.tr: Los principios son idénticos ya sea que el campo sea de 20 pies cuadrados o 2,000 acres.

segments.tr: إذا كان النبات مقاوماً بشكل طبيعي، أو كان مسبب المرض غائباً، أو كان الطقس جافاً جداً أو بارداً جداً، فإن المرض لا ينمو.

segments.src: This is the single most useful idea in all of plant protection, because it tells you exactly where to intervene: remove any one side of the triangle and you stop the disease.
segments.tr: هذه هي الفكرة الأكثر فائدة في كل حماية النبات، لأنها تخبرك بالضبط أين تتدخل: أزل أي جانب من أضلاع المثلث وستوقف المرض.

segments.src: **Transmission routes** — how pathogens travel — matter just as much as the pathogen itself.
segments.tr: **طرق الانتقال** — كيفية انتقال مسببات الأمراض — تهم تماماً كما يهم مسبب المرض نفسه.

segments.src: Spores blow in on the **wind**; bacteria splash from soil onto leaves in the **rain**; viruses ride inside **insect vectors**; and all three can travel on **infected seed, transplants, tools, boots, and irrigation water**.
segments.tr: تنجرف الأبواغ مع **الرياح**؛ وتتناثر البكتيريا من التربة على الأوراق في **المطر**؛ وتركب الفيروسات داخل **ناقلات حشرية**؛ ويمكن للثلاثة جميعاً أن تنتقل على **البذور المصابة والشتلات والأدوات والأحذية والمياه المروية**.

segments.src: Knowing the route tells you where to build a barrier.
segments.tr: معرفة المسار تخبرك أين تبني حاجزاً.

segments.src: A smart **control strategy** almost never relies on a single weapon.
segments.tr: استراتيجية **السيطرة** الذكية لا تعتمد تقريباً على سلاح واحد.

segments.src: Modern farming uses **Integrated Pest Management (IPM)** — layering several tactics so that no one method has to do all the work:
segments.tr: تستخدم الزراعة الحديثة **الإدارة المتكاملة للآفات (IPM)** — بطبقات عدة تكتيكات بحيث لا تضطر أي طريقة واحدة للقيام بكل العمل:

segments.src: 1. **Cultural control** — crop rotation, resistant varieties, proper spacing for airflow, and removing infected debris.
segments.tr: 1. **السيطرة الثقافية** — دوران المحاصيل والأصناف المقاومة والمسافات المناسبة لتدفق الهواء وإزالة الحطام المصاب.

segments.src: 2. **Physical/mechanical control** — clean seed, sanitized tools, mulches, and pulling out diseased plants.
segments.tr: 2. **السيطرة الفيزيائية/الميكانيكية** — البذور النظيفة والأدوات المعقمة والنشارة وسحب النباتات المريضة.

segments.src: 3. **Biological control** — beneficial microbes or insects that suppress the pathogen or its vector.
segments.tr: 3. **السيطرة البيولوجية** — الكائنات الدقيقة أو الحشرات المفيدة التي تثبط مسبب المرض أو ناقله.

segments.src: 4. **Chemical control** — fungicides or bactericides, used as a targeted last layer, not the first reflex.
segments.tr: 4. **السيطرة الكيميائية** — مبيدات فطرية أو بكتيرية، تستخدم كطبقة أخيرة موجهة، وليس كرد فعل أول.

segments.src: The goal is not to sterilize the field but to keep disease below the level where it hurts yield or quality.
segments.tr: الهدف ليس تعقيم الحقل بل الحفاظ على المرض تحت المستوى الذي يضر الإنتاجية أو الجودة.

segments.src: Picture a home gardener in Ohio growing tomatoes in a backyard raised bed.
segments.tr: تخيل بستاني منزلي في أوهايو يزرع الطماطم في سرير مرفوع في الفناء الخلفي.

segments.src: In late July, after a stretch of muggy, rainy days, the lower leaves show dark spots with yellow halos, then turn brown and drop.
segments.tr: في أواخر يوليو، بعد فترة من الأيام الرطبة والممطرة، تظهر الأوراق السفلى بقعاً غامقة مع هالات صفراء، ثم تصبح بنية اللون وتسقط.

segments.src: This is **early blight**, a fungal disease — a textbook case of the disease triangle snapping shut: a susceptible tomato (host), blight spores overwintering in the soil (pathogen), and warm, wet weather (environment).
segments.tr: هذا هو **اللفحة المبكرة**، مرض فطري — حالة كتابية من مثلث المرض الذي ينغلق: طماطم قابلة للإصابة (عائل)، وأبواغ اللفحة التي تشتو في التربة (مسبب المرض)، والطقس الدافئ الرطب (البيئة).

segments.src: Here is how IPM plays out on a small backyard budget, no lab required:
segments.tr: إليك كيف تسير IPM بميزانية صغيرة في الفناء الخلفي، لا توجد حاجة إلى معمل:

segments.src: - **Cultural:** Next season, plant the tomatoes in a different bed (rotation) and choose a blight-resistant variety at the local garden center. Space plants so air dries the leaves faster.
segments.tr: - **ثقافي:** في الموسم القادم، ازرع الطماطم في سرير مختلف (دوران) واختر صنفاً مقاوماً للفحة من مركز الحديقة المحلي. ضع النباتات بمسافات بحيث يجفف الهواء الأوراق بشكل أسرع.

segments.src: - **Physical:** Lay down mulch so rain does not splash soil-borne spores up onto the leaves, and water the roots — not the foliage — early in the day.
segments.tr: - **فيزيائي:** ضع النشارة بحيث لا يرتد المطر الأبواغ التي تحمل التربة على الأوراق، وسقي الجذور — وليس الأوراق — في وقت مبكر من اليوم.

segments.src: - **Biological/Chemical:** If it spreads, an approved garden fungicide labeled for tomato blight can protect the healthy upper leaves; always follow the label rate.
segments.tr: - **بيولوجي/كيميائي:** إذا انتشر، يمكن لمبيد فطري حديقة معتمد وموضح لفحة الطماطم أن يحمي الأوراق العليا الصحية؛ دائماً اتبع معدل العلامة.

segments.src: Scale that same thinking up and it is exactly what a commercial grower in California's Central Valley or an Iowa corn farmer does — just with weather forecasting, scouting reports, and disease-forecasting apps guiding the timing.
segments.tr: وسع نفس التفكير وهذا هو بالضبط ما يفعله مزارع تجاري في وادي كاليفورنيا المركزي أو مزارع ذرة في أيوا — فقط مع توقعات الطقس وتقارير التجول وتطبيقات التنبؤ بالأمراض التي توجه التوقيت.

segments.src: The principles are identical whether the field is 20 square feet or 2,000 acres.
segments.tr: المبادئ متطابقة سواء كان الحقل 20 قدماً مربعة أو 2,000 فدان.

segments.src: 1. Crop diseases are caused mainly by fungi, bacteria, and viruses, each with its own transmission route (wind, water/splash, insects, or contaminated seed and tools).
segments.tr: 1. تسببها أمراض المحاصيل بشكل أساسي الفطريات والبكتيريا والفيروسات، لكل منها طريقة انتقال خاصة بها (الرياح والماء/الرش والحشرات أو البذور والأدوات الملوثة).

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 مصطلحات اليوم

segments.src: - **Pathogen** — a disease-causing organism, such as a fungus, bacterium, or virus.
segments.tr: - **مسبب المرض** — كائن مسبب للمرض، مثل الفطر أو البكتيريا أو الفيروس.

segments.src: - **Disease triangle** — the principle that disease needs a susceptible host, a pathogen, and a favorable environment together.
segments.tr: - **مثلث المرض** — المبدأ القائل بأن المرض يحتاج إلى عائل قابل للإصابة ومسبب مرض وبيئة ملائمة معاً.

segments.src: - **Vector** — a carrier (often an insect like an aphid) that transmits a pathogen, especially viruses, from plant to plant.
segments.tr: - **الناقل** — حامل (غالباً حشرة مثل حشرة المن) ينقل مسبب المرض، خاصة الفيروسات، من نبات إلى آخر.

segments.src: - **Integrated Pest Management (IPM)** — a strategy that combines cultural, physical, biological, and chemical tactics to keep disease below a damaging level.
segments.tr: - **الإدارة المتكاملة للآفات (IPM)** — استراتيجية تجمع التكتيكات الثقافية والفيزيائية والبيولوجية والكيميائية للحفاظ على المرض تحت مستوى الضرر.

segments.src: - **Resistant variety** — a crop type bred to be less susceptible to a specific disease.
segments.tr: - **الصنف المقاوم** — نوع محصول تم تربيته ليكون أقل عرضة لمرض معين.

segments.tr: 2) X — خطأ؛ إذا كانت البيئة غير مناسبة، فإن أحد أضلاع مثلث المرض مفقود، لذا لا ينمو المرض.

fr.title: [Agriculture 101 #11] Pourquoi les cultures tombent-elles malades ? Un guide du terrain sur les maladies des plantes et leur contrôle

segments.src: > Plant diseases follow the same logic as human illness: a pathogen, a susceptible host, and the right conditions must line up — break any one link and the disease fails to spread.
segments.tr: > Les maladies des plantes suivent la même logique que les maladies humaines : un pathogène, un hôte vulnérable et les bonnes conditions doivent s'aligner — rompez l'un des maillons et la maladie ne se propage pas.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concept d'aujourd'hui

segments.src: When a tomato leaf develops brown spots or a wheat field turns rusty orange, that is a plant disease at work.
segments.tr: Quand une feuille de tomate développe des taches brunes ou qu'un champ de blé vire à l'orange rouillé, c'est une maladie des plantes à l'œuvre.

segments.src: Most crop diseases are caused by three main groups of **pathogens** (disease-causing organisms):
segments.tr: La plupart des maladies des cultures sont causées par trois groupes principaux de **pathogènes** (organismes causant des maladies) :

segments.src: - **Fungi** — by far the most common. They cause blights, mildews, rusts, and rots. Fungi love warm, humid, wet conditions and spread by microscopic spores.
segments.tr: - **Champignons** — de loin les plus courants. Ils causent des brûlures, des oïdiums, des rouilles et des pourritures. Les champignons aiment les conditions chaudes, humides et mouillées et se propagent par des spores microscopiques.

segments.src: - **Bacteria** — cause wilts, spots, and soft rots. They need a wound or a natural opening (like a leaf pore) to get in, and thrive in warm, wet weather.
segments.tr: - **Bactéries** — causent des flétrissements, des taches et des pourritures molles. Elles ont besoin d'une plaie ou d'une ouverture naturelle (comme un pore foliaire) pour entrer et prospèrent par temps chaud et humide.

segments.src: - **Viruses** — cause mottling, yellowing, and stunting. They cannot move on their own; they hitch a ride, usually inside an insect like an aphid, or on contaminated tools and hands.
segments.tr: - **Virus** — causent des mouchetures, un jaunissement et un rabougrissement. Ils ne peuvent pas se déplacer seuls ; ils se font transporter, généralement à l'intérieur d'un insecte comme un puceron, ou sur des outils et des mains contaminés.

segments.src: For any disease to actually happen, three things must come together at the same time.
segments.tr: Pour qu'une maladie se produise réellement, trois choses doivent se réunir en même temps.

segments.src: Plant scientists call this the **disease triangle**:
segments.tr: Les phytopathologistes appellent cela le **triangle de la maladie** :

segments.src: Susceptible host  +  Virulent pathogen  +  Favorable environment  =  Disease
segments.tr: Susceptible host  +  Virulent pathogen  +  Favorable environment  =  Disease

segments.src: If the plant is naturally resistant, or the pathogen is absent, or the weather is too dry or too cold, the disease does not develop.
segments.tr: Si la plante est naturellement résistante, ou si le pathogène est absent, ou si la météo est trop sèche ou trop froide, la maladie ne se développe pas.

segments.src: This is the single most useful idea in all of plant protection, because it tells you exactly where to intervene: remove any one side of the triangle and you stop the disease.
segments.tr: C'est l'idée la plus utile dans toute la protection des plantes, car elle vous dit exactement où intervenir : supprimez n'importe quel côté du triangle et vous arrêtez la maladie.

segments.src: **Transmission routes** — how pathogens travel — matter just as much as the pathogen itself.
segments.tr: **Les voies de transmission** — comment les pathogènes se déplacent — sont tout aussi importantes que le pathogène lui-même.

segments.src: Spores blow in on the **wind**; bacteria splash from soil onto leaves in the **rain**; viruses ride inside **insect vectors**; and all three can travel on **infected seed, transplants, tools, boots, and irrigation water**.
segments.tr: Les spores soufflent sur le **vent** ; les bactéries éclaboussent du sol sur les feuilles sous la **pluie** ; les virus se déplacent à l'intérieur de **vecteurs d'insectes** ; et les trois peuvent se propager via les **graines infectées, les plants, les outils, les bottes et l'eau d'irrigation**.

segments.src: Knowing the route tells you where to build a barrier.
segments.tr: Connaître la voie vous dit où construire une barrière.

segments.src: A smart **control strategy** almost never relies on a single weapon.
segments.tr: Une **stratégie de lutte** intelligente ne repose presque jamais sur une seule arme.

segments.src: Modern farming uses **Integrated Pest Management (IPM)** — layering several tactics so that no one method has to do all the work:
segments.tr: L'agriculture moderne utilise la **Gestion intégrée des ravageurs (GIR)** — en superposant plusieurs tactiques de sorte qu'aucune méthode n'ait à faire tout le travail :

segments.src: 1. **Cultural control** — crop rotation, resistant varieties, proper spacing for airflow, and removing infected debris.
segments.tr: 1. **Lutte culturale** — rotation des cultures, variétés résistantes, espacement approprié pour la circulation de l'air, et élimination des débris infectés.

segments.src: 2. **Physical/mechanical control** — clean seed, sanitized tools, mulches, and pulling out diseased plants.
segments.tr: 2. **Lutte physique/mécanique** — graines propres, outils désinfectés, paillis et arrachage des plantes malades.

segments.src: 3. **Biological control** — beneficial microbes or insects that suppress the pathogen or its vector.
segments.tr: 3. **Lutte biologique** — microbes ou insectes bénéfiques qui suppriment le pathogène ou son vecteur.

segments.src: 4. **Chemical control** — fungicides or bactericides, used as a targeted last layer, not the first reflex.
segments.tr: 4. **Lutte chimique** — fongicides ou bactéricides, utilisés comme une couche finale ciblée, et non comme le premier réflexe.

segments.src: The goal is not to sterilize the field but to keep disease below the level where it hurts yield or quality.
segments.tr: L'objectif n'est pas de stériliser le champ mais de maintenir la maladie en dessous du niveau où elle nuit au rendement ou à la qualité.

segments.tr: ## Dans la vie quotidienne

segments.src: Picture a home gardener in Ohio growing tomatoes in a backyard raised bed.
segments.tr: Imaginez un jardinier amateur en Ohio cultivant des tomates dans un bac surélevé de jardin.

segments.src: In late July, after a stretch of muggy, rainy days, the lower leaves show dark spots with yellow halos, then turn brown and drop.
segments.tr: Fin juillet, après une période de jours moites et pluvieux, les feuilles inférieures montrent des taches sombres avec des halos jaunes, puis brunissent et tombent.

segments.src: This is **early blight**, a fungal disease — a textbook case of the disease triangle snapping shut: a susceptible tomato (host), blight spores overwintering in the soil (pathogen), and warm, wet weather (environment).
segments.tr: Ceci est le **mildiou précoce**, une maladie fongique — un cas d'école du triangle de la maladie se refermant : une tomate vulnérable (hôte), des spores de mildiou hivernant dans le sol (pathogène), et une météo chaude et humide (environnement).

segments.src: Here is how IPM plays out on a small backyard budget, no lab required:
segments.tr: Voici comment la GIR se joue avec un petit budget de jardin, sans laboratoire requis :

segments.src: - **Cultural:** Next season, plant the tomatoes in a different bed (rotation) and choose a blight-resistant variety at the local garden center. Space plants so air dries the leaves faster.
segments.tr: - **Culturale:** La saison prochaine, plantez les tomates dans un autre bac (rotation) et choisissez une variété résistante au mildiou au centre-jardin local. Espacez les plantes pour que l'air sèche les feuilles plus rapidement.

segments.src: - **Physical:** Lay down mulch so rain does not splash soil-borne spores up onto the leaves, and water the roots — not the foliage — early in the day.
segments.tr: - **Physique:** Posez du paillis pour que la pluie ne projette pas les spores du sol sur les feuilles, et arrosez les racines — non le feuillage — tôt le matin.

segments.src: - **Biological/Chemical:** If it spreads, an approved garden fungicide labeled for tomato blight can protect the healthy upper leaves; always follow the label rate.
segments.tr: - **Biologique/Chimique:** S'il se propage, un fongicide de jardin approuvé étiqueté pour le mildiou des tomates peut protéger les feuilles supérieures saines ; suivez toujours le dosage indiqué sur l'étiquette.

segments.src: Scale that same thinking up and it is exactly what a commercial grower in California's Central Valley or an Iowa corn farmer does — just with weather forecasting, scouting reports, and disease-forecasting apps guiding the timing.
segments.tr: Agrandissez cette même réflexion et c'est exactement ce qu'un producteur commercial dans la vallée centrale de Californie ou un agriculteur de maïs de l'Iowa fait — avec simplement des prévisions météorologiques, des rapports de scouting et des applications de prévision de maladies guidant le timing.

segments.tr: Les principes sont identiques que le champ fasse 20 pieds carrés ou 2 000 acres.

pt.title: [Agriculture 101 #11] Por Que as Culturas Adoecem? Um Guia Prático de Doenças das Plantas e Seu Controle

segments.src: > Plant diseases follow the same logic as human illness: a pathogen, a susceptible host, and the right conditions must line up — break any one link and the disease fails to spread.
segments.tr: > As doenças das plantas seguem a mesma lógica que as doenças humanas: um patógeno, um hospedeiro suscetível e as condições corretas devem se alinhar — interrompa qualquer um dos elos e a doença não se propaga.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de Hoje

segments.src: When a tomato leaf develops brown spots or a wheat field turns rusty orange, that is a plant disease at work.
segments.tr: Quando uma folha de tomate desenvolve manchas marrons ou um campo de trigo fica laranja enferrujado, essa é uma doença das plantas em ação.

segments.src: Most crop diseases are caused by three main groups of **pathogens** (disease-causing organisms):
segments.tr: A maioria das doenças das culturas é causada por três grupos principais de **patógenos** (organismos causadores de doenças):

segments.src: - **Fungi** — by far the most common. They cause blights, mildews, rusts, and rots. Fungi love warm, humid, wet conditions and spread by microscopic spores.
segments.tr: - **Fungos** — de longe os mais comuns. Eles causam requeimas, míldios, ferrugens e podridões. Os fungos adoram condições quentes, úmidas e molhadas e se propagam por esporos microscópicos.

segments.src: - **Bacteria** — cause wilts, spots, and soft rots. They need a wound or a natural opening (like a leaf pore) to get in, and thrive in warm, wet weather.
segments.tr: - **Bactérias** — causam murchas, manchas e podridões moles. Elas precisam de uma ferida ou uma abertura natural (como um poro da folha) para entrar e prosperam em clima quente e úmido.

segments.src: - **Viruses** — cause mottling, yellowing, and stunting. They cannot move on their own; they hitch a ride, usually inside an insect like an aphid, or on contaminated tools and hands.
segments.tr: - **Vírus** — causam moteamento, amarelecimento e nanismo. Eles não podem se mover por conta própria; dependem de um carona, geralmente dentro de um inseto como um afídeo, ou em ferramentas e mãos contaminadas.

segments.src: For any disease to actually happen, three things must come together at the same time.
segments.tr: Para que qualquer doença realmente aconteça, três coisas devem se unir ao mesmo tempo.

segments.src: Plant scientists call this the **disease triangle**:
segments.tr: Os cientistas de plantas chamam isso de **triângulo da doença**:

segments.src: Susceptible host  +  Virulent pathogen  +  Favorable environment  =  Disease
segments.tr: Susceptible host  +  Virulent pathogen  +  Favorable environment  =  Disease

segments.src: If the plant is naturally resistant, or the pathogen is absent, or the weather is too dry or too cold, the disease does not develop.
segments.tr: Se a planta é naturalmente resistente, ou o patógeno está ausente, ou o clima é muito seco ou muito frio, a doença não se desenvolve.

segments.src: This is the single most useful idea in all of plant protection, because it tells you exactly where to intervene: remove any one side of the triangle and you stop the disease.
segments.tr: Essa é a ideia mais útil em toda a proteção de plantas, porque lhe diz exatamente onde intervir: remova qualquer um dos lados do triângulo e você detém a doença.

segments.src: **Transmission routes** — how pathogens travel — matter just as much as the pathogen itself.
segments.tr: **Rotas de transmissão** — como os patógenos viajam — importam tanto quanto o próprio patógeno.

segments.src: Spores blow in on the **wind**; bacteria splash from soil onto leaves in the **rain**; viruses ride inside **insect vectors**; and all three can travel on **infected seed, transplants, tools, boots, and irrigation water**.
segments.tr: Os esporos voam no **vento**; bactérias respingam do solo para as folhas na **chuva**; vírus viajam dentro de **vetores de insetos**; e todos os três podem viajar em **sementes infectadas, mudas, ferramentas, botas e água de irrigação**.

segments.src: Knowing the route tells you where to build a barrier.
segments.tr: Conhecer a rota lhe diz onde construir uma barreira.

segments.src: A smart **control strategy** almost never relies on a single weapon.
segments.tr: Uma **estratégia de controle** inteligente quase nunca depende de uma única arma.

segments.src: Modern farming uses **Integrated Pest Management (IPM)** — layering several tactics so that no one method has to do all the work:
segments.tr: A agricultura moderna usa **Manejo Integrado de Pragas (MIP)** — combinando várias táticas para que nenhum método tenha que fazer todo o trabalho:

segments.src: 1. **Cultural control** — crop rotation, resistant varieties, proper spacing for airflow, and removing infected debris.
segments.tr: 1. **Controle cultural** — rotação de culturas, variedades resistentes, espaçamento adequado para circulação de ar e remoção de detritos infectados.

segments.src: 2. **Physical/mechanical control** — clean seed, sanitized tools, mulches, and pulling out diseased plants.
segments.tr: 2. **Controle físico/mecânico** — sementes limpas, ferramentas sanitizadas, coberturas de solo e remoção de plantas doentes.

segments.src: 3. **Biological control** — beneficial microbes or insects that suppress the pathogen or its vector.
segments.tr: 3. **Controle biológico** — microrganismos benéficos ou insetos que suprimem o patógeno ou seu vetor.

segments.src: 4. **Chemical control** — fungicides or bactericides, used as a targeted last layer, not the first reflex.
segments.tr: 4. **Controle químico** — fungicidas ou bactericidas, usados como uma camada final direcionada, não o primeiro reflexo.

segments.src: The goal is not to sterilize the field but to keep disease below the level where it hurts yield or quality.
segments.tr: O objetivo não é esterilizar o campo, mas manter a doença abaixo do nível em que prejudica a produção ou a qualidade.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Na Vida Cotidiana

segments.src: Picture a home gardener in Ohio growing tomatoes in a backyard raised bed.
segments.tr: Imagine um jardineiro caseiro em Ohio cultivando tomates em uma cama elevada no quintal.

segments.src: In late July, after a stretch of muggy, rainy days, the lower leaves show dark spots with yellow halos, then turn brown and drop.
segments.tr: No final de julho, após um período de dias úmidos e chuvosos, as folhas inferiores mostram manchas escuras com halos amarelos, depois ficam marrons e caem.

segments.src: This is **early blight**, a fungal disease — a textbook case of the disease triangle snapping shut: a susceptible tomato (host), blight spores overwintering in the soil (pathogen), and warm, wet weather (environment).
segments.tr: Esta é a **requeima inicial**, uma doença fúngica — um caso de manual do triângulo da doença se fechando: um tomateiro suscetível (hospedeiro), esporos de requeima hibernando no solo (patógeno) e clima quente e úmido (ambiente).

segments.src: Here is how IPM plays out on a small backyard budget, no lab required:
segments.tr: Veja como o MIP funciona com um pequeno orçamento caseiro, sem laboratório necessário:

segments.src: - **Cultural:** Next season, plant the tomatoes in a different bed (rotation) and choose a blight-resistant variety at the local garden center. Space plants so air dries the leaves faster.
segments.tr: - **Cultural:** Na próxima estação, plante os tomates em uma cama diferente (rotação) e escolha uma variedade resistente à requeima no centro de jardinagem local. Afaste bem as plantas para que o ar seque as folhas mais rápido.

segments.src: - **Physical:** Lay down mulch so rain does not splash soil-borne spores up onto the leaves, and water the roots — not the foliage — early in the day.
segments.tr: - **Físico:** Coloque cobertura de solo para que a chuva não respingue esporos do solo nas folhas e regue as raízes — não a folhagem — no início do dia.

segments.src: - **Biological/Chemical:** If it spreads, an approved garden fungicide labeled for tomato blight can protect the healthy upper leaves; always follow the label rate.
segments.tr: - **Biológico/Químico:** Se se propagar, um fungicida de jardim aprovado e indicado para requeima de tomate pode proteger as folhas superiores saudáveis; sempre siga a dosagem indicada no rótulo.

segments.src: Scale that same thinking up and it is exactly what a commercial grower in California's Central Valley or an Iowa corn farmer does — just with weather forecasting, scouting reports, and disease-forecasting apps guiding the timing.
segments.tr: Aplique esse mesmo pensamento em escala maior e é exatamente o que um produtor comercial no Vale Central da Califórnia ou um agricultor de milho de Iowa faz — apenas com previsão de tempo, relatórios de monitoramento e aplicativos de previsão de doenças orientando o timing.

segments.src: The principles are identical whether the field is 20 square feet or 2,000 acres.
segments.tr: Os princípios são idênticos se o campo tem 20 metros quadrados ou 2.000 acres.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumo em 3 Linhas

segments.src: 1. Crop diseases are caused mainly by fungi, bacteria, and viruses, each with its own transmission route (wind, water/splash, insects, or contaminated seed and tools).
segments.tr: 1. As doenças das culturas são causadas principalmente por fungos, bactérias e vírus, cada um com sua própria rota de transmissão (vento, água/respingo, insetos ou sementes e ferramentas contaminadas).

segments.src: 2. Disease only occurs when a susceptible host, an active pathogen, and a favorable environment overlap — the "disease triangle."
segments.tr: 2. A doença ocorre apenas quando um hospedeiro suscetível, um patógeno ativo e um ambiente favorável se sobrepõem — o "triângulo da doença".

segments.src: 3. The best defense is Integrated Pest Management: layer cultural, physical, biological, and chemical tactics rather than relying on any single one.
segments.tr: 3. A melhor defesa é o Manejo Integrado de Pragas: combine táticas culturais, físicas, biológicas e químicas em vez de depender de apenas uma.

in.title: [Agriculture 101 #11] Mengapa Tanaman Sakit? Panduan Lapangan terhadap Penyakit Tanaman dan Pengendaliannya

segments.src: > Plant diseases follow the same logic as human illness: a pathogen, a susceptible host, and the right conditions must line up — break any one link and the disease fails to spread.
segments.tr: > Penyakit tanaman mengikuti logika yang sama seperti penyakit manusia: patogen, inang yang rentan, dan kondisi yang tepat harus bersatu — putuskan salah satu tautan dan penyakit gagal menyebar.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: When a tomato leaf develops brown spots or a wheat field turns rusty orange, that is a plant disease at work.
segments.tr: Ketika daun tomat berkembang dengan bintik-bintik cokelat atau ladang gandum berubah menjadi oranye berkarat, itu adalah penyakit tanaman yang sedang bekerja.

segments.src: Most crop diseases are caused by three main groups of **pathogens** (disease-causing organisms):
segments.tr: Sebagian besar penyakit tanaman disebabkan oleh tiga kelompok utama **patogen** (organisme penyebab penyakit):

segments.src: - **Fungi** — by far the most common. They cause blights, mildews, rusts, and rots. Fungi love warm, humid, wet conditions and spread by microscopic spores.
segments.tr: - **Jamur** — sejauh ini yang paling umum. Mereka menyebabkan layu, tepung putih, karat, dan pembusukan. Jamur menyukai kondisi hangat, lembab, basah dan menyebar melalui spora mikroskopis.

segments.src: - **Bacteria** — cause wilts, spots, and soft rots. They need a wound or a natural opening (like a leaf pore) to get in, and thrive in warm, wet weather.
segments.tr: - **Bakteri** — menyebabkan layu, bintik-bintik, dan pembusukan lunak. Mereka membutuhkan luka atau bukaan alami (seperti pori daun) untuk masuk, dan berkembang dalam cuaca hangat dan basah.

segments.src: - **Viruses** — cause mottling, yellowing, and stunting. They cannot move on their own; they hitch a ride, usually inside an insect like an aphid, or on contaminated tools and hands.
segments.tr: - **Virus** — menyebabkan bercak-bercak, menguning, dan kerdil. Mereka tidak dapat bergerak sendiri; mereka menumpang, biasanya di dalam serangga seperti kutu daun, atau pada alat dan tangan yang terkontaminasi.

segments.src: For any disease to actually happen, three things must come together at the same time.
segments.tr: Agar penyakit benar-benar terjadi, tiga hal harus bersatu pada saat yang bersamaan.

segments.src: Plant scientists call this the **disease triangle**:
segments.tr: Para ilmuwan tanaman menyebutnya **segitiga penyakit**:

segments.src: Susceptible host  +  Virulent pathogen  +  Favorable environment  =  Disease
segments.tr: Susceptible host  +  Virulent pathogen  +  Favorable environment  =  Disease

segments.src: If the plant is naturally resistant, or the pathogen is absent, or the weather is too dry or too cold, the disease does not develop.
segments.tr: Jika tanaman secara alami tahan, atau patogen tidak ada, atau cuaca terlalu kering atau terlalu dingin, penyakit tidak berkembang.

segments.src: This is the single most useful idea in all of plant protection, because it tells you exactly where to intervene: remove any one side of the triangle and you stop the disease.
segments.tr: Ini adalah ide paling berguna dalam semua perlindungan tanaman, karena memberitahu Anda dengan tepat di mana untuk campur tangan: hilangkan salah satu sisi segitiga dan Anda menghentikan penyakit.

segments.src: **Transmission routes** — how pathogens travel — matter just as much as the pathogen itself.
segments.tr: **Rute transmisi** — cara patogen bepergian — sama pentingnya dengan patogen itu sendiri.

segments.src: Spores blow in on the **wind**; bacteria splash from soil onto leaves in the **rain**; viruses ride inside **insect vectors**; and all three can travel on **infected seed, transplants, tools, boots, and irrigation water**.
segments.tr: Spora terbang dalam **angin**; bakteri menciprat dari tanah ke daun dalam **hujan**; virus naik di dalam **vektor serangga**; dan ketiganya dapat bepergian pada **benih terinfeksi, bibit, alat, sepatu bot, dan air irigasi**.

segments.src: Knowing the route tells you where to build a barrier.
segments.tr: Mengetahui rute memberi tahu Anda di mana harus membangun penghalang.

segments.src: A smart **control strategy** almost never relies on a single weapon.
segments.tr: Strategi **pengendalian** yang cerdas hampir tidak pernah mengandalkan satu senjata.

segments.src: Modern farming uses **Integrated Pest Management (IPM)** — layering several tactics so that no one method has to do all the work:
segments.tr: Pertanian modern menggunakan **Manajemen Hama Terpadu (IPM)** — menglapisi beberapa taktik sehingga tidak ada satu metode yang harus melakukan semua pekerjaan:

segments.src: 1. **Cultural control** — crop rotation, resistant varieties, proper spacing for airflow, and removing infected debris.
segments.tr: 1. **Pengendalian budaya** — rotasi tanaman, varietas tahan, jarak yang tepat untuk aliran udara, dan menghilangkan puing-puing yang terinfeksi.

segments.src: 2. **Physical/mechanical control** — clean seed, sanitized tools, mulches, and pulling out diseased plants.
segments.tr: 2. **Pengendalian fisik/mekanis** — benih bersih, alat yang disinfeksi, mulsa, dan mencabut tanaman yang sakit.

segments.src: 3. **Biological control** — beneficial microbes or insects that suppress the pathogen or its vector.
segments.tr: 3. **Pengendalian biologis** — mikroba bermanfaat atau serangga yang menekan patogen atau vektornya.

segments.src: 4. **Chemical control** — fungicides or bactericides, used as a targeted last layer, not the first reflex.
segments.tr: 4. **Pengendalian kimia** — fungisida atau bakterisida, digunakan sebagai lapisan terakhir yang ditargetkan, bukan refleks pertama.

segments.src: The goal is not to sterilize the field but to keep disease below the level where it hurts yield or quality.
segments.tr: Tujuannya bukan untuk mensterilkan ladang tetapi untuk menjaga penyakit di bawah tingkat di mana ia merusak hasil atau kualitas.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: Picture a home gardener in Ohio growing tomatoes in a backyard raised bed.
segments.tr: Bayangkan seorang tukang kebun rumahan di Ohio menanam tomat di tempat tidur yang ditinggikan di halaman belakang.

segments.src: In late July, after a stretch of muggy, rainy days, the lower leaves show dark spots with yellow halos, then turn brown and drop.
segments.tr: Pada akhir Juli, setelah serangkaian hari yang lembab dan hujan, daun-daun yang lebih rendah menunjukkan bintik-bintik gelap dengan lingkaran kuning, kemudian menjadi cokelat dan jatuh.

segments.src: This is **early blight**, a fungal disease — a textbook case of the disease triangle snapping shut: a susceptible tomato (host), blight spores overwintering in the soil (pathogen), and warm, wet weather (environment).
segments.tr: Ini adalah **layu awal**, penyakit jamur — kasus buku teks dari segitiga penyakit yang menutup rapat: tomat yang rentan (inang), spora layu yang melewati musim dingin di tanah (patogen), dan cuaca hangat dan basah (lingkungan).

segments.src: Here is how IPM plays out on a small backyard budget, no lab required:
segments.tr: Berikut adalah bagaimana IPM memainkan peran pada anggaran halaman belakang yang kecil, tidak ada lab yang diperlukan:

segments.src: - **Cultural:** Next season, plant the tomatoes in a different bed (rotation) and choose a blight-resistant variety at the local garden center. Space plants so air dries the leaves faster.
segments.tr: - **Budaya:** Musim depan, tanam tomat di tempat tidur yang berbeda (rotasi) dan pilih varietas tahan layu di pusat taman lokal. Jarak tanaman sehingga udara mengeringkan daun lebih cepat.

segments.src: - **Physical:** Lay down mulch so rain does not splash soil-borne spores up onto the leaves, and water the roots — not the foliage — early in the day.
segments.tr: - **Fisik:** Letakkan mulsa sehingga hujan tidak menciprat spora yang dibawa tanah ke daun, dan air akar — bukan dedaunan — awal hari.

segments.src: - **Biological/Chemical:** If it spreads, an approved garden fungicide labeled for tomato blight can protect the healthy upper leaves; always follow the label rate.
segments.tr: - **Biologis/Kimia:** Jika menyebar, fungisida taman yang disetujui berlabel untuk layu tomat dapat melindungi daun atas yang sehat; selalu ikuti tingkat label.

segments.src: Scale that same thinking up and it is exactly what a commercial grower in California's Central Valley or an Iowa corn farmer does — just with weather forecasting, scouting reports, and disease-forecasting apps guiding the timing.
segments.tr: Skalakan pemikiran yang sama dan itu persis apa yang dilakukan oleh petani komersial di Central Valley California atau petani jagung Iowa — hanya dengan peramalan cuaca, laporan pengintaian, dan aplikasi peramalan penyakit memandu waktu.

segments.src: The principles are identical whether the field is 20 square feet or 2,000 acres.
segments.tr: Prinsip-prinsipnya identik apakah bidangnya 20 kaki persegi atau 2.000 hektar.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Ringkasan 3 Baris

segments.src: 1. Crop diseases are caused mainly by fungi, bacteria, and viruses, each with its own transmission route (wind, water/splash, insects, or contaminated seed and tools).
segments.tr: 1. Penyakit tanaman disebabkan terutama oleh jamur, bakteri, dan virus, masing-masing dengan rute transmisi sendiri (angin, air/cipratan, serangga, atau benih dan alat yang terkontaminasi).
